preamble: In the Moldavian dialect of Romanian, labials are palatalized before front vowels, and the palatalized bilabial [pʲ] then shifts its closure from the lips to the palate, becoming the palatal stop [c] (spelled ch). The voiced [bʲ] and the nasal [mʲ] develop the same way, to [ɟ] and [ɲ]. The result is a well-known stereotype of Moldavian speech, absent from standard Romanian. No comparable regular pʲ > c change has been verified outside Moldavian Romanian.

examples.note: The from-form is the conservative pronunciation kept in Standard Romanian. Wikipedia transcribes the result as [koˈkʲil] and also records [kop̚ˈkʲil] with a residual labial closure.
